2020_152_task_force_return_to_school_aug.paragraph: Slide presentation delivered to the Troy Board of Education on August 5, 2020, reporting the work of the district Return to Learn task forces organized around the MI Return to School Road Map. Four workgroups covering safety protocols, operations, instruction, and mental health and social-emotional well-being present recommendations for the 2020-21 school year, including universal masking, cleaning and screening protocols, and a redesigned secondary 3x3 block schedule. The core instructional design is a single daily schedule that works identically across Michigan Safe Start Phases 1 through 6, supported by 1:1 iPads for all students in grades K-12 and delivery through Schoology and Zoom. A special Board meeting on Wednesday, August 12 was scheduled to approve the plan.
2020_152_task_force_return_to_school_aug.page:
**Meeting and framing**
Presented at the Troy School District Board of Education meeting of August 5, 2020, under the banner Return to Learn and anchored to the MI Return to School Road Map, described as built by public health experts and flexible to changing conditions.

**Goals and guiding principles**
Goals: students return to face-to-face instruction as soon as possible; safety and sustainability; consistent programming. Guiding principles: Troy teachers lead learning; build classroom communities; attend to social/emotional needs; maximum flexibility for families; collaborative effort.

**Task force structure**

| Strand | Leads |
| --- | --- |
| Safety Protocols | Rick West and Jordan Harris |
| Operations | Rick West and Jordan Harris |
| Instruction | Kris Griffor and Christine DiPilato |
| Mental Health and Social Emotional Well-Being | Jessica Carrier |

**Safety and operations**
Masks required for all school staff, visitors, and all students on buses, inside buildings, and anywhere on school grounds when individuals may be within 6 feet; all students K-Post High required to wear masks all day. Exceptions cover incapacitation, inability to remove a mask unaided, an approved medical or behavioral health exemption with a physician note, eating or drinking, and outdoor strenuous physical activity with social distancing. Supplies cited: 5,000 adult disposable masks on hand with 50,000 on order, 52,000 kid-size disposable masks on order, and 4,300 face shields on hand. Hand-washing for at least 20 seconds is encouraged; frequently touched surfaces sanitized between classes, at least every 4 hours, and at day's end. More than $10 million has been invested in HVAC systems in the past 7 years. Elementary classroom workspaces shown 6 feet apart; a high school classroom 3 feet apart. Student lockers prohibited in grades 6-12; three Registered Nurses available for COVID-19 response. Staff and students stay home with a fever of 100.4 degrees or more; guidance follows the Oakland County Health Division, MDHHS, and CDC.

**Instructional plan**
Three scenarios align to state phases: Virtual Learning (Phases 1-3, schools closed to student attendance, 100% virtual); Transition to Return Plan (Phases 4/5, 50% of students in-seat and 50% virtual, cohorted by last name, buildings open 4 days with all students virtual Wednesdays); and In-Seat Learning Plan (Phases 4/5/6, 100% of students in-seat, buildings open 5 days). All three use 3 periods per day and 90-minute class periods with live instruction via Zoom. Return to regularly scheduled programming is listed as September 2021.

**Technology**
The Board voted to move forward with 1:1 iPads for all students in grades K-12, with a keyboard, and an iPad kit for every teacher including interactive stylus, keyboard, and stand for live capture. Schoology is the learning management system K-12; Zoom is the virtual delivery platform. There will be no separate stand-alone virtual program.

**Schedules**
Secondary moves to an A Day (hours 1-3) / B Day (hours 4-6) rotation with 90-minute blocks, 20-minute advisory, and 60-minute student support or teacher collaboration blocks; classes meet 5 times over a two-week rotation. First class starts at regular times: HS 7:20, Early MS 7:54, Late MS 8:19. During 50% attendance, last names A-K attend in person Monday and Tuesday and L-Z attend Thursday and Friday, with all students virtual Wednesday.

**Start of year and next steps**
Tuesday 9/1 is the first day for K, 6, and 9 only; 9/2 and 9/3 are half days by cohort; 9/4 no school; 9/7 Labor Day; 9/8 first full day. Next steps: staff Q&A Thursday, presentation to parents Thursday, a Return to Learn Community Conversation Monday, August 10 live on Facebook, and a special Board meeting Wednesday, August 12 to approve the plan.
2020_152_task_force_return_to_school_aug.verbose:
Return to Learn presentation made to the Troy School District Board of Education at its meeting of August 5, 2020, reporting the recommendations of the district's task forces working under the MI Return to School Road Map, which the slides characterize as developed with public health experts and flexible to changing conditions.

GOALS AND GUIDING PRINCIPLES. The stated goals are that students return to face-to-face instruction as soon as possible, safety and sustainability, and consistent programming. The guiding principles are that Troy teachers lead learning, build classroom communities, attend to social/emotional needs, provide maximum flexibility for families, and work as a collaborative effort.

TASK FORCE ORGANIZATION. Four strands are identified with their leads: Safety Protocols and Operations under Rick West and Jordan Harris; Instruction under Kris Griffor and Christine DiPilato; and Mental Health and Social Emotional Well-Being under Jessica Carrier.

SOCIAL/EMOTIONAL TEAM MEMBERS. Jesse Allgeier (Counselor), Jackie Cheyne (Counselor), Lara Dixon (Principal), Elizabeth Gumbis (Teaching and Learning), David Guzak (Social Worker), Jordan Harris (Employee Services), Grace Lynch (Early Childhood), Matt Jansen (Principal), Christian Mueller (Principal), Stacey Schoenherr (Social Worker), Sara Ventimiglio (Psychologist), with team leader Jessica Carrier.

SAFETY AND OPERATIONS TEAM MEMBERS. Dominick Asaro (Transportation Liaison), Rob Carson (Director, Maintenance and Operations), Jason Cichowicz (TEA Vice President, 5th Grade Teacher, Schroeder Elementary), Tammy DiPonio (Principal, Costello Elementary), Melanie Harper (Speech Pathologist / Parent), Jordan Harris (Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services), Judy Holmes (Executive Secretary to the Superintendent), Kathy Kochanski (Transportation Manager, First Student), Tony Lucci (TEA President), Jennifer Martus (TESA President, Secretary, Costello Elementary), Gayle Moran (Food Service Liaison), Tony Morse (Principal, Boulan Park Middle School), Kristy Pierce (Assistant Principal, Boulan Park Middle School), Nancy Richter (TESPA President, Paraprofessional, Athens High School), Remo Roncone (Principal, Troy High), Christin Silagy (Director, ELD and Federal Grants / Parent), Rick West (Assistant Superintendent, Business Services), Sara Young (Supervisor, Special Education), Brian Zawislak (Assistant Principal, Troy High), and Tim Fulcher (Director, Athletics).

INSTRUCTION TASK FORCE MEMBERS. The instruction rosters name, among others, Lindsey Becker (Baker), Erich Beregszaszy (Athens), Ryan Brinks (IAE Associate Principal), Adam Burns (Athens), Dina Chrisopoulos (Athens), Casey Conaton (Baker, AP), Jonathan Cross (Baker, Principal), Melissa Curth (Troy High, AP), Amy Dent (Athens), Lara Dixon (Athens, AP), Bob Dowd (Athens, Principal), Joseph Duda (Larson, Principal), Lisa Dziatczak (TCT, Supervisor), Gareth Eve (Smith), Christine Foren (Supervisor, SE), Krysta Gentilini (TCCHS), Laura Guzowski (Boulan Park), Natalie Haezebrouck (Director, T&L), Joe Havrilla (Coordinator, Instrumental Music), Dan House (Troy High, AP), Stephanie Hyska (ELD), Toni Isaac (Troy High), Ron Keoleian (Curriculum), Cindy Larson, Philip Lewan (Boulan Park), Tony Lucchi (TEA President), Alan Macnair (Troy High), Carol Machak (Athens), Kristin Martin (Athens, AP), Jonathan Matthews (TCCHS), Nichole Mayes (IAE), Kim McKinnon (Athens), Stacey Miller (Athens), Christian Mueller (Smith, Principal), Michael Munaco (Athens, AP), Trevor Potts (Larson), Kathleen Rainey (Curriculum), Kathryn Robles (Troy High), Kendall Rock (Boulan Park), Evan Rokicki (Curriculum Specialist), Remo Roncone (Troy High), Christin Silagy (Director, ELD), Julie Tucker (Troy High), Charlie Tull (Larson), Bill Turner (Director, TCCHS), Kimberly Vergauwen (Smith, AP), Kelsey Witt (Curriculum Specialist), Marie Woodman (Curriculum), Hadeel Yousif (Larson), and Brian Zawislak (Troy High, AP). Elementary instruction team members listed include Julia Alder, Eric Andary, Michelle Barsh, Jennifer Bell, Scott Binford, Jaclyn Botsford, Joyce Brasington, Brian Canfield, Jessica Carrier, Jason Cichowicz, Euginia Connell, Michael Cottone, Erin Detmer, Tammy DiPonio, Lauren Fragomeni, Emily Freeman, Lisa Georges, Scott Germansky, Sarah Glasser, Jamie Grant, Natalie Haezebrouck, Joe Havrilla, Lauren Henderson, Katherine Hosbach, Matt Jansen, Ron Keoleian, Elliott Kern, Erin Keyser, Sarah Kijek, Robin MacLeish, Aaron Maliepaard, Lisa McDonald, Grayson McKinney, Kristy Menghini, Melanie Morey, Rebecca Morrow, Kelly Pasternak, Shari Pawlus, Kris Piotrowski, Jennifer Reis, Kyle Rogers, Zachary Rondot, Julieann Schiepke, Lauren See, Jaynie Sorenson, Corrien Spurin, Rosanne Thomas, Matthew Tignanelli, Jeremy Whan, Kelsey Witt, Marie Woodman, Sarah Young, and Stephanie Zendler.

MENTAL HEALTH AND SEL. Supports for students and families include a student self-report mental health survey, the district screener SRSS administered three times a year, daily check-ins, the ONETroy Community Resources Document, staff and family resources, and TSD Cares on-line resources. Staff supports include a staff self-awareness survey, wellness resources, district and building support systems, the Employee Assistance Program, staff development in trauma, socio-emotional learning and equity and inclusion, and protocols for responding to student concerns or crisis at the building level.

PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT. Masks must be worn by all school staff, visitors, and all students on buses or other transportation, inside school buildings, and anywhere on school grounds including outside when individuals may be within 6 feet of each other. All students K-Post High are required to wear masks all day, in classrooms as well as common areas. Exceptions are someone incapacitated or unconscious, someone unable to remove a mask without assistance, someone approved for a medical or behavioral health exemption with a physician note, anyone eating or drinking, and students in outdoor strenuous physical activity while practicing social distancing. Masks are subject to the Troy School District dress code. Disposable masks will be available on buses and in buildings: 5,000 adult disposable masks on hand with 50,000 on order, and 52,000 kid-size disposable masks on order. Disposable gloves will be available in buildings; 4,300 face shields are on hand; safety barriers are being explored for specific spaces and protective wear such as gowns for specific classrooms.

CLEANING AND HYGIENE. Students are encouraged to wash hands for at least 20 seconds often, after using the bathroom and before eating or drinking. Frequently touched surfaces will be sanitized between classes, at least every 4 hours, and at the end of the day; student desks cleaned between use. Sanitizer stations will be available throughout each building and checklists used to confirm stations and soap dispensers are filled and sinks working. On HVAC systems, the district reports investing more than $10 million in the past 7 years into reliable and safe systems at all school buildings, with routine filter changes.

SPACING, MOVEMENT AND ACCESS. Classroom seating will be separated as much as possible and/or face the same direction; elementary workspaces shown are 6 feet apart and a high school classroom is shown at 3 feet apart. Visitors are limited to essential functions, must call the office for entry, and are screened with a temperature check and questionnaire. Assemblies, field trips, and similar large-group activities are temporarily prohibited. Floor and wall markings, signage, and one-way hallway traffic are planned. Students are encouraged to bring their own water bottles. The district will have access to three (3) Registered Nurses to assist with COVID-19 response. Soft furnishings that cannot easily be disinfected will be removed from classrooms, and use of student lockers is prohibited in grades 6-12.

SCREENING AND POSITIVE CASES. Staff self-screen daily; a parent or guardian is expected to screen students daily. Staff and students should stay home if ill or with a fever of 100.4 degrees or more. Anyone who thinks or knows they have COVID-19 or had direct exposure should stay home and contact the building office, with next steps guided by the Oakland County Health Division, MDHHS, and CDC guidelines through the District Nurse Consultant. A student who becomes ill at school will be isolated in a designated area with a designated staff member until picked up by an authorized person. A person with an alternative diagnosis who is symptom-free and fever-free for 24 hours without fever-reducing medication may return. The Oakland County Health Department will notify schools of confirmed positive cases and close contacts will be notified as soon as possible; privacy of staff and students will be respected.

FOOD SERVICE, ATHLETICS, TRANSPORTATION. Indoor assemblies bringing together more than one classroom are prohibited; cafeterias and other large areas such as gymnasiums, media centers, and LGI rooms will be used for lunch, outdoor areas used where possible, menu items limited and most lunches prepackaged, meals available for virtual student pick-up, and lunch periods altered to reduce classes per period. Athletics will comply with all MHSAA guidance. Bus transportation is available within transportation boundaries; hand sanitizer is required before boarding with stations at each bus entrance, face coverings required, buses disinfected, and windows kept open weather permitting. Building-level administration has received a list of medically vulnerable students flagged in their building; virtual learning options are available to all families and medical plans on file may be updated.

SAFETY PROTOCOLS BY PHASE AND CHALLENGES. Phases 1-3 mean no in-person instruction. Phases 4, 5 and 6 carry face coverings for all staff and students, social distancing, no visitors in buildings, transportation with face coverings, modified lunch and recess, and strict cleaning and hygiene protocols. Major challenges listed are lack of guidance from the Oakland County Health Division on screening and response to positive tests, social distancing in classrooms, common areas and buses, cleaning of desks between use, lunch services, and budget uncertainties.

INSTRUCTIONAL SCENARIOS. Virtual Learning applies to Phases 1-3 with schools closed for student attendance, 3 periods per day, 90-minute class periods, live Zoom instruction for all courses, and 100% virtual attendance. The Transition to Return Plan applies to Phases 4/5 with 50% of students in-seat and 50% virtual, 3 periods per day, 90-minute classes, live instruction in person and via Zoom, cohorting by last name, buildings open 4 days for in-seat attendance, and all students virtual on Wednesdays. The In-Seat Learning Plan applies to Phases 4/5/6 with 100% of students in-seat, buildings open all 5 days. Return to regularly scheduled programming is listed as September 2021. Families may elect to keep students home to learn virtually all year or send them on the day aligned to student last name.

TECHNOLOGY. The Board voted to move forward with 1:1 iPads for all students in grades K-12; every student will have a dedicated device and keyboard, and every teacher an iPad kit including interactive stylus, keyboard and stand for live capture. Schoology is the K-12 learning management system and Zoom the virtual delivery platform. There will be no separate stand-alone virtual learning program.

SCHEDULES. Elementary components: literacy and math taught daily, science and social studies several times per week, access to all specials virtually, and built-in student support. Secondary components: A Day equals hours 1-3, B Day equals hours 4-6, 90-minute instructional blocks, student advisory, and student support. In the virtual secondary week, each day runs three 90-minute blocks with breaks, a 20-minute advisory, and either 60 minutes of student support or 60 minutes of teacher team collaboration and professional learning; first class starts in alignment with regular school start times of HS 7:20, Early MS 7:54, and Late MS 8:19. Classes meet 5 times over a two-week rotation. Stated benefits include one daily schedule that transitions across Phases 1-6, deeper 90-minute learning, adaptable passing time, a reduction in hall passing from 5 times to 2 times, HS starting at regular time and dismissing before lunch, and extended MS lunchtime for safety protocols; instructional considerations note comparable time in class versus a 6-period day, slightly less time per week but fewer transitions.

TRANSITION SCHEDULES. Under the Transition to Return Plan, teachers teach in the classroom daily with live capture via Zoom and interactive capability, attendance taken daily, last names A-K in seat Monday and Tuesday while L-Z attend virtually, last names L-Z in seat Thursday and Friday while A-K attend virtually, and all students virtual on Wednesday. The draft early middle school 50% in-seat schedule runs 1st or 4th hour (95 minutes) 7:55-9:30, 10-minute passing, 2nd or 5th hour (90) 9:40-11:10, 10-minute passing, 3rd or 6th hour (90) with lunch (25) 11:20-1:15, advisory (20) 1:25-1:45, buses at 1:45, and virtual student support or teacher collaboration 1:45-2:45; Wednesday runs 3rd hour (90) 11:20-12:50, teacher lunch 12:50-1:15, and student support and intervention 1:00-2:20. The draft high school 50% in-seat schedule runs 1st or 4th hour (95) 7:20-8:55, 2nd or 5th hour (95) 9:00-10:35, 3rd or 6th hour (95) 10:40-12:15, grab-to-go lunch with buses at 12:25, teacher duty-free lunch 12:20-12:45, advisory 12:50-1:10 (20 minutes) by appointment, and student support and intervention or teacher collaboration 1:10-2:20; Wednesday shifts to 2nd hour 9:05-10:40, 3rd hour 10:50-12:25, teacher lunch 12:30-1:00, and student support and intervention 1:00-2:20.

SPECIAL PROGRAMS. Troy College and Career High School aligns with the 3x3 block in an ABAB rotation, adds a morning session for student support and small group work, and moves first bell to a later 9:00 a.m. start, with additional information from Mr. Turner. International Academy East cites unique program needs, IB course requirements, three campuses, an A/B day rotation, in-seat determination by grade level (9/10 and 11/12), a virtual start on 8/20, and transition to in-seat courses on 8/31 in alignment with the TSD decision. For IFSP, IEP and 504 students from birth through post-high, the Roadmap highlights plans covering special education, birth-to-five services at the Early Childhood Center and Post-High at TCT, structures for general and special education teacher collaboration on assessments and instruction outlined in IEPs, assistive technologies, and continuation-of-service plans for social work, occupational, physical, and speech and language therapy including evaluations. Troy School District preschool programs will follow state and county guidance in accordance with licensing rules, prioritize students in seats for family supports, and offer virtual programming options.

WEEK ONE AND NEXT STEPS. Tuesday 9/1 is the first day for K, 6 and 9 only with orientation activities and afternoon teacher professional development; Wednesday 9/2 is an A Day half day for A-K in person with L-Z virtual; Thursday 9/3 is a B Day half day for L-Z in person with A-K virtual; Friday 9/4 is no school; Monday 9/7 is Labor Day; and Tuesday 9/8 is the first full day of school. The September calendar shown for 50% in-seat attendance marks the first day as 6th and 9th only, with all students virtual on Wednesdays September 16, 23 and 30. Next steps listed are a staff Q&A on Thursday, distribution of the presentation to parents Thursday with a question submission form, a Return to Learn Community Conversation on Monday, August 10 live on Facebook, a special Board meeting Wednesday, August 12 to approve the plan, and parents indicating interest in 100% virtual learning beginning Thursday the 13th with flexibility to make changes.

2020_153_troy_school_district_covid_19_p.paragraph: COVID-19 Preparedness and Response Plan for the Troy School District dated August 12, 2020, filed under Governor Whitmer's Executive Order 2020-142 and covering instruction, mental health, face coverings, hygiene, cleaning, athletics, screening, testing, and busing across the phases of the Michigan Safe Start Plan. The plan records the district address as 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, district code number 63150, with Oakland Schools as the intermediate school district and the Troy Board of Education as the authorizing body. It was adopted by the Board at a special meeting held August 12, 2020, and was due to the State Superintendent and State Treasurer and posted to the district website by August 17, 2020.
2020_153_troy_school_district_covid_19_p.page:
**Identification**
Name of District: Troy School District. Address: 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. District Code Number: 63150. Web address: www.troy.k12.mi.us. Intermediate School District: Oakland Schools. Authorizing Body: Troy Board of Education. Plan dated August 12, 2020. Submitted by Richard M. Machesky, EdD., Superintendent of Schools.

**Legal framework**
Governor Whitmer's Executive Order 2020-142 requires districts to adopt a COVID-19 Preparedness and Response Plan across the phases of the Michigan Safe Start Plan, with the Michigan Return to School Roadmap supplying phase-appropriate safety protocols. Assurances include in-person instruction for students with disabilities consistent with their IEPs, good-faith equal access to alternative modes of instruction for students with disabilities from birth through age 26 including auxiliary services under section 1296 of the Revised School Code, MCL 380.1296, compliance with U.S. Department of Education and Michigan Department of Education guidance, individualized determinations on compensatory services for 2019-2020 closures, closure of buildings in Phases 1-3 except for defined personnel and licensed child-care providers, suspension of athletics and busing in Phases 1-3, continued employee pay, continued food distribution, and a Phase 4 prohibition on indoor assemblies bringing together students from more than one classroom.

**Instruction**
The task force totaled more than 105 members drawn from teachers, administrators, union representatives, and central office. Instructional elements include an updated pacing guide in Schoology, collaboration and professional learning time, MTSS team communication on each student's plan, monthly collaboration for general and special education teams on caseload students, and district MTSS expectations for new or in-process evaluation packets. Professional learning includes a Summer Homegrown Institute on anti-racist teaching, building community, and digital teaching, plus August grade-level learning on transitions between face-to-face and remote. All students K-12 will be provided an iPad; teachers receive an iPad kit; Schoology and ZOOM are the platforms. Scenarios mirror the Return to Learn plan: virtual in Phases 1-3, 50% in-seat in Phases 4/5, and 100% in-seat in Phases 4/5/6, with a return to regularly scheduled programming in September 2021.

**Health protocols**

| Area | Key requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Face coverings | Required at all times except eating; medical exemption needs a physician note, is logged in a master database, and is marked by an ID sticker |
| Hygiene | Posted classroom hygiene protocols, daily supply checks, first-day handwashing instruction reinforced weekly |
| Cleaning | EPA-approved disinfectant or diluted bleach; high-frequency areas wiped every four hours with time, date and initials charted; desks wiped after each exit or period |
| Screening | Isolation room no smaller than 100 square feet; trained quarantine officer; 5-minute interval activity log; 48-hour contact recall prioritizing sustained contact of 15 minutes or more |
| Exclusion | Staff positive test means 10 days from symptom onset plus 24 hours fever-free; close contacts excluded 14 days |
| Busing | Sanitizer mounts at each bus entrance, disposable masks at the door, ID sticker system, windows open when above 55 degrees F |

**Athletics**
Follows MHSAA guidelines and State of Michigan orders. Physicals on file for 2019-2020 carry over with an MHSAA questionnaire via FinalForms; Dr. Moeller recommends a physical and an electrocardiogram for any athlete proven to have had COVID-19. Practices use a 5-question survey, temperature check, masks, and 6 feet of distance. Low-risk sports (boys tennis, cross country with a maximum 70 runners, girls golf with a maximum 72 competitors at an 18-hole site, girls swim and dive) begin outdoor practices August 12; football began August 10 helmets-only with full pads August 17; MHSAA decisions on competition timelines were expected on or by August 20. Currently 100 spectators allowed, home-team only, no charge for entry, with games in stadiums and gyms live streamed through Pixellot/NFHS Network.

**Submission**
Due to the Board for approval by August 15 or seven days before the first day of school, adopted August 12, 2020, and transmitted by the ISD to the State Superintendent of Public Instruction and State Treasurer and posted to the district home page no later than August 17, 2020.
2020_153_troy_school_district_covid_19_p.verbose:
COVID-19 Preparedness and Response Plan of the Troy School District, dated August 12, 2020, prepared to satisfy Governor Whitmer's Executive Order 2020-142 and titled internally TROY SCHOOL DISTRICT RETURN TO LEARN 2020-2021.

DISTRICT IDENTIFICATION. Name of District: Troy School District. Address of District: 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. District Code Number: 63150. Web address: www.troy.k12.mi.us. Name of Intermediate School District: Oakland Schools. Name of Authorizing Body: Troy Board of Education. Name of District leader submitting the plan: Richard M. Machesky, EdD., Superintendent of Schools.

INTRODUCTION. Executive Order 2020-142 provides a structure to support all schools in Michigan as they plan for a return of pre-K-12 education in the fall; under the order districts must adopt a COVID-19 Preparedness and Response Plan describing how they will cope with the disease across the phases of the Michigan Safe Start Plan, with the Michigan Return to School Roadmap offering a guide to safety protocols appropriate during each phase. The order notes there is no one-size-fits-all solution, that what works in Lansing may not work in Sault Sainte Marie, and that districts retain flexibility to tailor instruction to their needs and regional disease conditions.

ASSURANCES. The district agrees to meet the requirements of Executive Order 2020-142, assuring that when it provides in-person instruction to students without disabilities it will also provide in-person instruction to students with disabilities consistent with their individualized education programs; that when schools are closed to in-person instruction it will strive in good faith and to the extent practicable, based on available resources, technology, training and curriculum, to provide equal access to alternative modes of instruction to students with disabilities from birth through age 26, including auxiliary services under section 1296 of the Revised School Code, MCL 380.1296; that during any state of emergency or disaster related to the pandemic it will comply with guidance from the United States Department of Education including its Office of Civil Rights and Office of Special Education and Rehabilitative Services, and the Michigan Department of Education; that it will make individualized determinations on compensatory services for students with disabilities in light of the 2019-2020 school-year closures; that during Phases 1, 2 or 3 it will close buildings to anyone except district employees or contractors necessary for minimum basic school operations, food-service workers preparing food for distribution to students or families, and licensed child-care providers and the families they serve following state emergency protocols; that during Phases 1, 2 or 3 it will suspend athletics, after-school activities, inter-school activities and busing; that during those phases it will continue pay of school employees while redeploying staff, subject to collective bargaining agreements; that it will continue food distribution to eligible students; that during Phase 4 it will prohibit indoor assemblies bringing together students from more than one classroom; and that it will cooperate with the local public health department on confirmed cases, collecting contact information for close contacts from two days before symptoms to the time the individual was last present in school.

PHASE FRAMEWORK. The MI Safe Start Plan remains the highest-level governing framework. Schools may not provide in-person instruction of any kind in Phases 1-3; all schools may resume in-person instruction beginning in Phase 4; some regulations relax in Phase 5; and schools remain open with some lasting safety requirements in Phase 6. Schools retain authority to enact stricter public health requirements and to close buildings even if not mandated. Tribal Education Agencies and non-public schools are exempt from many state regulations but must adhere to Roadmap health and safety protocols. Phases 1-3 describe increasing and substantial community spread, concern about health system capacity, and testing and tracing that may be insufficient. Phase 4 describes falling new cases and deaths with case levels still high, most new outbreaks quickly identified, traced and contained, health system capacity able to handle outbreaks, and continued need for distancing. Phase 5 describes continued decreases, less common community infection, lower positivity rates with widespread testing, and rapid case investigation and containment.

INSTRUCTION. The district's goal is to have students return to face-to-face instruction as soon as possible while ensuring safety and sustainability with consistent programming, with Troy teachers leading learning and building nurturing classroom communities. The task force team included teachers, administrators, union representatives, and central office members totaling more than 105 members. Key instructional elements are an updated pacing guide and resources posted in Schoology; collaboration and professional learning time for teachers around curriculum and best practices; MTSS teams communicating on each student's plan to determine need and design plans; monthly collaboration time for general education and special education teacher teams regarding caseload students; and a district MTSS team creating expectations for receiving new packets or reviewing packets that were in process for evaluation for learning gaps. Professional learning includes the Summer Homegrown Institute on anti-racist teaching, building community and digital teaching, plus August grade-level professional learning on seamless transitions between face-to-face and remote experiences. Communication and family supports include Schoology as the consistent K-12 platform, opportunities for families to request translation services virtually, and parent training in Schoology and ZOOM.

TECHNOLOGY SUPPORT. All students K-12 will be provided with an iPad for at-home learning. Every teacher will have a dedicated iPad kit of tools including interactive stylus, keyboard and stand for live capture. K-12 instructional delivery is integrated into Schoology as the learning management system and ZOOM as the virtual platform. Technology gives students and families who choose or are scheduled to stay home direct access to the classroom through ZOOM; the virtual learning plan is connected to the in-seat plan with students logging in to their classroom through ZOOM, and there will be no separate, stand-alone virtual learning program.

SCENARIOS. Virtual Learning aligns to Phases 1-3, with 3 periods per day, live instruction via Zoom, and 100% virtual attendance. The Transition to Return Plan aligns to Phases 4/5 with 50% of students in-seat and 50% virtual, 3 periods per day, 90-minute classes for secondary, cohorting for in-seat attendance, buildings open 4 days for in-seat attendance, and all students attending virtually on Wednesdays. The In-Seat Learning Plan aligns to Phases 4/5/6 with 100% of students in-seat, 3 periods per day, 90-minute secondary classes, live instruction in person and via zoom, and buildings open for in-seat attendance all 5 days. Return to regularly scheduled programming is listed as September 2021. Elementary schedule components are literacy and math daily, science and social studies several times per week, access to all specials virtually, and built-in student support for at-risk learners and students with 504s and IEPs. Secondary components are an A Day (hours 1-3) / B Day (hours 4-6) schedule, 90-minute instructional blocks, student advisory, and student support for at-risk learners and students with 504s and IEPs. Notable virtual changes for Fall 2020 are a consistent schedule PreK through Post High, daily live Zoom instruction by all teachers, daily attendance, and regular student feedback PreK through Post High with academic grades in grades 6-12.

MENTAL AND SOCIAL EMOTIONAL HEALTH (PHASES 1-5). Schools will use the Student Risk Screening Survey (SRSS) three times per year to assess behavioral needs, with data reviewed by district and school MTSS teams and action plans created. Students will participate in a self-reporting universal mental health screener, and guidelines for identification and rapid referral of at-risk students are communicated to building-level support teams. Professional development for 2020-21 includes training in mental wellness, trauma informed teaching, student social emotional learning, and equity and inclusion, occurring over the course of the year. A School Mental Health professional is designated as the main contact to centralize mental health referrals and family communication, and also serves as liaison to local agencies and community partners. Compiled wellness resources include documents on student wellness and social emotional supports for families, the TSD Cares on-line referral for assistance, staff wellness resources, and the Employee Assistance Program (EAP). Crisis response is housed at the building level and includes grief and loss support; the School Mental Health building team will work with staff during staff meetings and establish a forum for staff wellness.

FACE COVERINGS. Staff, students and visitors must wear face coverings at all times except for eating, a requirement to be included in parent communications, handbooks, student orientations and staff orientations between August 1 and August 30. Students and parents must watch a safety video on wearing and maintaining face coverings and sign off before students may enter the classroom on the first day. Staff and students are expected to provide their own coverings; disposable coverings will be ordered and provided to anyone who forgets or cannot provide their own, with supply placed on buses and in each building by custodial and transportation staff by August 30. Individuals claiming medical exemption must provide their building office with a physician's note; exempted individuals will be recorded in a master database and issued a sticker for their student or staff ID. Staff will define, teach and prompt mask wearing within predictable school routines with daily re-teaching until routines are established. Students requiring special considerations such as 504 Plans, IEPs or health care plans will be referred to their case manager for additional interventions. Guests such as presenters and substitute teachers receive a disposable covering at sign-in, and non-compliance results in the guest being escorted from the building by the building administrator or law enforcement officer.

HYGIENE. Buildings will have adequate hand washing and hand sanitizer stations; supplies including paper towels, soap, hand sanitizer, tissues and trash receptacles are checked daily and restocked in classrooms, with teachers contacting the office immediately if supplies run low. Each classroom will post a hygiene protocol with a hand-washing schedule and a room and materials cleaning schedule. Teachers or the school nurse teach proper handwashing and cough and sneeze etiquette on the first day of school, reinforced weekly or more often, possibly by video. The Operations Department procures soap, hand sanitizer, paper towels and tissues routinely, posts signage, monitors supplies, and procures hand sanitizing stations in collaboration with building leadership.

CLEANING. District-level administrators and building operations will review guidance and the Building Operations sections of the MI Safe Schools: Michigan's 2020-21 Return to School Roadmap. An inventory of cleaning supplies compliant with EPA-approved COVID-19 materials will be taken and orders placed. All buildings receive EPA-approved disinfectant or diluted bleach solution, paper towels, face shields and gloves; staff or students must wear gloves, a mask and face shield when cleaning. Each building custodial team and administrator will tour the building, identify frequent-use areas, and create a map kept secure in the head custodian room and office for use by custodial substitutes. Custodial staff will wipe all high-frequency usage areas every four hours and following any evening activities, noting time, date and initials on a daily chart. Student desks will be wiped every time students exit the room at elementary level, or after every period at secondary level, with EPA-approved disinfectant or diluted bleach solution accessible from each classroom.

ATHLETICS. The plan follows all MHSAA-recommended guidelines and State of Michigan orders. Student-athletes with a sports physical on file for 2019-2020 do not need a new physical for 2020-2021 but must complete the MHSAA sports questionnaire on FinalForms and submit it to their coach or athletic trainer before practice or tryouts; those without a physical on file must complete and print the form from FinalForms. As recommended by Dr. Moeller, any student-athlete proven to have had COVID-19 should have a sports physical and an electrocardiogram (ECG) to rule out myocarditis, with full recommendations on both high school athletic websites and sent to parents on voluntary summer practice rosters. Practice check-in follows summer workout procedures: a 5-question survey, temperature check, masks worn by all student-athletes and coaches during check-in, and 6 feet of distance before and after practice. Masks must be worn before and after practice and equipment cleaned during and after. Only the football team has limited locker room use due to equipment needs, with players reporting dressed; all other teams report ready, and bathrooms are used one at a time. The weight room remains closed until allowed to open by the Governor, weights may be used outdoors and must be cleaned between use. Athletes bring their own water bottles with no sharing, no hydration stations and no snacks; no spectators at practice. For games, all athletes, coaches and game workers follow the same check-in, coaches, workers and bench personnel wear masks, visiting teams do not use locker rooms, only the home football team has limited locker room use, and players bring their own water or small disposable bottles are provided with a trained adult in PPE operating any water station. Concession stands are a local health department decision. If parents are not allowed to attend games, two-way busing will be provided; student-athletes may drive themselves with parent permission and a signed release, and parents may drive their child to an away game. Clarification was pending from the Governor on how cheerleaders and marching band members count toward maximum capacity. Under OAA rules, spectators are a home team decision, only home team spectators would be allowed, currently 100 spectators are allowed, the plan is for no charge for entry, and all games played in stadiums and gyms will be live streamed through Pixellot/NFHS Network.

COVID POSITIVE PROTOCOL. A more complete version appears on page five of the MHSAA sports return to play documents. Steps: contact the building administrator, central office administrator and health department and follow guidance; close contacts may have to quarantine for 14 days, with close contact defined as anyone less than six feet apart for more than 15 minutes at any point from two days before symptoms until the individual is isolated; notify all schools, families and officials involved without identifying the person; monitor those present but not in close contact for symptoms, who may not need testing; and clean the area.

FALL SPORTS GUIDANCE. Low-risk sports: boys tennis begins outdoor practices August 12 with no more than four teams at one site (JV and varsity count as two teams) and larger invitationals likely canceled; cross country begins August 12 with a maximum of 70 runners allowed in a race and spectator capacity difficult to monitor; girls golf begins August 12 with a maximum of 72 competitors at an 18-hole site; girls swim and dive begins outdoor practices August 12 pending the Governor on indoor training, with no more than four teams at one site. Moderate- and high-risk sports: boys soccer begins August 12 with no more than four teams at one site and an MHSAA decision on competition timelines anticipated on or by August 20; boys water polo is not an MHSAA sport and was moved to spring by the MWPA; football begins practices August 10 with helmets only for an acclimation week, permits 7 on 7, handoffs, blocking pads and sleds, allows full pads beginning August 17, with an MHSAA timeline decision anticipated on or by August 20; sideline cheer begins outdoor practice August 12 with its counting toward stadium capacity undetermined; volleyball begins outdoor practices August 12 pending the Governor on indoor training, with no more than four teams at one site. Regional and state meets were being investigated by MHSAA for several sports.

SCREENING AND TESTING. The district will comply with the health, screening and testing guidance and requirements of the Oakland County COVID-19 Public Health Toolkit for K-12 Schools. All school staff and students must conduct a health safety self-assessment at home before coming to work. Each building will identify a remote and secluded room no smaller than 100 square feet as an isolation area outfitted with appropriate PPE, and will have an identified and trained quarantine officer whose duties take precedence over other responsibilities. From identification of potential infection the student will not be left unattended, with a log sheet of activity maintained at 5-minute intervals until the student or staff member is safely removed. Parent communication is immediate with directions on pick-up and testing; designated office staff contact the family daily until test results are provided and verified before return. During quarantine the student self-identifies locations and individuals contacted over the past 48 hours, prioritizing sustained contact of 15 minutes or more; the health department is contacted after parents to assist with contact tracing. Staff unable to work due to symptoms must report it, with the school health official or Employee Services Department monitoring daily and directing testing. A positive test for a staff member requires quarantine away from school for 10 days since symptoms first appeared, 24 hours with no fever, and improvement of symptoms. Household members, classmates and teachers of the quarantined person who are close contacts are excluded for 14 days after their last date of close contact.

BUSING AND STUDENT TRANSPORTATION. All transportation companies supporting the district will be contacted to confirm receipt of the MI Safe Schools Roadmap criteria; a meeting will review Phase 4 criteria; contracting companies will sign an assurance statement; and contracts will be altered as needed to address cleaning, sanitizing and professional development. The transportation department will assess the number of buses on the road. Buses will be fitted with mounts for hand sanitizer at the entrance. Contractors will use CDC-compliant cleaning supplies between routes including frequent-contact areas, and disposable face masks will be placed at the bus entrance each morning. A mandatory face covering policy for buses will be communicated to families, if medically feasible, unless it is determined case by case that it is not safe for the bus driver to wear a facial covering. Bus drivers will be informed of the ID badge sticker system for students medically unable to wear a mask, and all students will show their ID as they board. Driver training covers appropriate use of face covering, policies on face covering and hand sanitizing, and cleaning and disinfecting methods. Weather permitting, defined as no precipitation and temperature above 55 degrees F, drivers will keep windows open en route and when stopped. On buses with specialized transportation and equipment needs, aides or drivers will wipe down equipment before use.

SUBMISSION. Each district must submit a single completed Assurance Document and Preparedness Plan to its Board of Education in time for approval by August 15 or seven days before the first day of school, whichever comes first. This plan was adopted by the Troy School District Board of Education at a Special Board Meeting held on August 12, 2020, with signature lines for the Board of Education President and date. The Preparedness Plan will be collected by the Intermediate School District for transmission to the State Superintendent of Public Instruction and State Treasurer by August 17, 2020, and must be posted on the district's public website home page no later than August 17, 2020, with a single application filed by the district rather than multiple applications for individual schools.

2020_154_5a_m072120bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education meeting of July 21, 2020, held remotely via Zoom videoconference and presented as consent item 5.A. on the August 18, 2020 agenda. The Board adopted seven resolutions on unanimous 7-0 roll call votes, including a consent agenda, a two-year administrative contract for David Recker as Principal of Hamilton Elementary School, contract extensions for principals, directors and assistant superintendents through June 30, 2022, and an extension of the Superintendent's contract from July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2025. The Board also adopted a Pledge for Racial Equity and named the renovated ITT Building at 1522 E. Big Beaver Road the Troy School District Learning Center.

**Meeting**
Troy Board of Education meeting of July 21, 2020, held remotely via Zoom Video Conferencing with public notice posted to allow community participation. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m.; the meeting adjourned at 8:40 p.m. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, and carried as item 5.A. on the 08.18.20 agenda.

**Attendance**
In addition to Mr. Schmidt, Board members Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson were present. Also present: Superintendent Machesky; administrators DiPilato, Carrier, Griffor, Birmingham, Haezebrouck, Harris, DiPonio, Detmer, Keyser, Barsh, Recker, Cottone, Morey and West; and six other members of the audience. Recognition, additions and deletions, public communication, curriculum and business items were all reported as none.

**Actions**

| Res. | Subject | Moved / Supported | Vote |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 20-059 | Consent agenda items A-F | Hauff / Philippart | 7-0 |
| 20-060 | Two-year administrative contract without tenure, David Recker, Principal, Hamilton Elementary School | Wilson / Hammond | 7-0 |
| 20-061 | Extension of administrator contracts through June 30, 2022 | Philippart / Wilson | 7-0 |
| 20-062 | Extension of assistant superintendent contracts through June 30, 2022 | Anne / Gottlieb | 7-0 |
| 20-063 | Extension of Superintendent contract, July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2025 | Gottlieb / Anne | 7-0 |
| 20-064 | Pledge for Racial Equity | Philippart / Hauff | 7-0 |
| 20-065 | Naming of the ITT Building | Wilson / Anne | 7-0 |

**Consent agenda contents**
Minutes of the June 9, 2020 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the June 16, 2020 Special Board of Education Meeting and Closed Session; minutes of the June 16, 2020 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report for May 2020; Michigan High School Athletic Association (MHSAA) Membership Resolution 2020/2021; and second reading and adoption of the Equity and Excellence Policy.

**Contract extensions**
Resolution 20-061 extended contracts through June 30, 2022, or as otherwise indicated in the individual contract, without tenure in the administrative positions and subject to the layoff provision in the Administrative Handbook. Resolution 20-062 extended the contracts of Rick West, Kris Griffor, Christine DiPilato and Jordan Harris, all assistant superintendents, through June 30, 2022 without tenure.

**Pledge for Racial Equity**
The pledge commits the district to holding conversations about racism, diversity, equity and inclusion; to implementing and expanding implicit bias education; and to sharing both best and unsuccessful practices, creating accountability systems to measure, monitor and evaluate progress, and sharing regular updates with the Equity Office of the Michigan Department of Civil Rights.

**Naming of the ITT Building**
Citing that the Niles Center housing Community Education, Adult Education and Alternative Education has come to the end of its useful life, that in September 2019 the Board resolved to purchase and renovate 1522 E. Big Beaver Road, Troy, Michigan, Sidwell No. 20-26-200-055, that renovations have been ongoing since February 2020 with an August 2020 opening scheduled, and that Board Policy 6000.08 leaves school naming to the Board, the building was named the Troy School District Learning Center, commonly the Troy Learning Center or TLC.

**Superintendent update and announcements**
Dr. Machesky updated the Board on Return to School planning and the Michigan Return to School Roadmap developed by the Governor's office, noting task force teams were preparing recommendations for Board review the week of August 3rd. Mr. Schmidt announced a special meeting on Wednesday, August 5th at 4:30 p.m. via Zoom and the next regular Board meeting on August 18th at 7:00 p.m., also via Zoom.
2020_154_5a_m072120bdmtg.verbose:
Official minutes of the Troy Board of Education meeting held July 21, 2020, appearing as agenda item 5.A. for the meeting of 08.18.20. The meeting was held remotely via Zoom Video Conferencing, with a public notice posted to allow community members to participate remotely.

CALL TO ORDER AND ATTENDANCE. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, present were Board members Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, and Wilson. Also present were Superintendent Machesky; administrators DiPilato, Carrier, Griffor, Birmingham, Haezebrouck, Harris, DiPonio, Detmer, Keyser, Barsh, Recker, Cottone, Morey, and West; and six other members of the audience. Recognition, additions and deletions, and public communication were each recorded as none, as were curriculum and business items later in the meeting.

RESOLUTION 20-059, CONSENT AGENDA. Moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Dr. Philippart, resolved that the Troy Board of Education approve items A, B, C, D, E, and F on the consent agenda: A, minutes of the June 9, 2020 Board of Education Workshop; B, minutes of the June 16, 2020 Special Board of Education Meeting and Closed Session; C, minutes of the June 16, 2020 Board of Education Meeting; D, Treasurer's Report for May 2020; E, Michigan High School Athletic Association (MHSAA) Membership Resolution 2020/2021; and F, second reading and adoption of the Equity and Excellence Policy. Roll call vote: Wilson yes, Anne yes, Gottlieb yes, Hammond yes, Hauff yes, Philippart yes, Schmidt yes. Yes: 7. No: 0.

RESOLUTION 20-060, ADMINISTRATIVE APPOINTMENT. Moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Mrs. Hammond, resolved that the Board of Education issue a two-year administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Mr. David Recker, who will begin his duties as Principal of Hamilton Elementary School commencing with the 2020-21 school year. Roll call vote: Anne yes, Gottlieb yes, Hammond yes, Hauff yes, Philippart yes, Schmidt yes, Wilson yes. Yes: 7. No: 0.

RESOLUTION 20-061, EXTENSION OF ADMINISTRATIVE AND PERSONNEL CONTRACTS. Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Dr. Wilson, resolved that the Troy Board of Education approve the extension of the contracts of the named administrators through June 30, 2022, or as otherwise indicated in the administrator's individual contract, without tenure in the administrative positions and subject to the layoff provision in the Administrative Handbook where applicable and as permitted by law. The administrators named are Ryan Brinks, Associate Principal, International Academy-East; Lara Dixon, Principal, Athens High School; Remo Roncone, Principal, Troy High School; Jonathan Cross, Baker Middle School; Joe Duda, Principal, Larson Middle School; Anthony Morse, Boulan Park Middle School; Christian Mueller, Smith Middle School; Michelle Barsh, Principal, Martell Elementary School; Joyce Brasington, Principal, Wattles Elementary School; Brian Canfield, Principal, Schroeder Elementary School; Mike Cottone, Principal, Troy Union Elementary School; Erin Detmer, Principal, Leonard Elementary School; Tammy DiPonio, Principal, Costello Elementary School; Matt Jansen, Principal, Wass Elementary School; Melanie Morey, Principal, Barnard Elementary School; Shari Pawlus, Hill Elementary School; Jeremey Whan, Principal, Bemis Elementary School; Stephanie Zendler, Principal, Morse Elementary School; Melissa Curth, Assistant Principal, Troy High School; Robert Dowd, Assistant Principal, Athens High School; Dan House, Assistant Principal, Troy High School; Kristin Martin, Assistant Principal, Athens High School; Michael Munaco, Assistant Principal, Athens High School; Brian Zawislak, Assistant Principal, Troy High School; Cassandra Conaton, Assistant Principal, Baker Middle School; Kristy Pierce, Assistant Principal, Boulan Park Middle School; Kimberly Vergauwen, Assistant Principal, Smith Middle School; Kerry Birmingham, Director, Communications and Strategic Initiatives; Jessica Carrier, Director, Special Education; Rob Carson, Director, Maintenance and Operations; and Sarah Young, Supervisor, Special Education. Roll call vote: Gottlieb yes, Hammond yes, Hauff yes, Philippart yes, Schmidt yes, Wilson yes, Anne yes. Yes: 7. No: 0.

RESOLUTION 20-062, EXTENSION OF ASSISTANT SUPERINTENDENT CONTRACTS. Moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mr. Gottlieb, resolved that the Troy Board of Education approve the extension of the contracts for Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services; Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction; Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Instruction; and Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services, through June 30, 2022, without tenure in the administrative positions. Roll call vote: Hammond yes, Hauff yes, Philippart yes, Schmidt yes, Wilson yes, Anne yes, Gottlieb yes. Yes: 7. No: 0.

RESOLUTION 20-063, SUPERINTENDENT CONTRACT. Moved by Mr. Gottlieb and supported by Mrs. Anne, resolved that the Troy Board of Education extend the contract of the Superintendent of Schools, to be in effect from July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2025, without tenure in the administrative position and subject to provisions of the written Agreement. Roll call vote: Hauff yes, Philippart yes, Schmidt yes, Wilson yes, Anne yes, Gottlieb yes, Hammond yes. Yes: 7. No: 0.

RESOLUTION 20-064, PLEDGE FOR RACIAL EQUITY. Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mr. Hauff. The pledge recites three commitments. First, that the Troy School District will continue to make communities and workplaces trusting places by having complex, and sometimes difficult, conversations about racism, diversity, equity and inclusion, creating and maintaining environments, platforms and forums where residents feel comfortable reaching out to colleagues to gain greater awareness of each other's experiences and perspectives, encouraging ongoing dialogue and not tolerating incongruence with these values of openness, thereby building trust, encouraging compassion and open-mindedness, and reinforcing a commitment to a culture of inclusivity that acknowledges racism as real and pursues equity through racially conscious approaches. Second, that the district will implement and expand implicit bias education, noting that the field of implicit bias reminds us that we all have unconscious biases and that such education enables individuals and institutions to recognize, acknowledge and engage in debiasing strategies, with a commitment to rolling out or expanding implicit bias education within local municipalities and institutions to help employees, students and residents recognize blind spots. Third, that the district will share best and unsuccessful practices, since many local jurisdictions are at different stages in increasing racial consciousness and cultural awareness, committing to identify best successes and least successful initiatives to share with others, to create accountability systems within communities and institutions to measure, monitor and evaluate progress, and to share regular updates with the Equity Office of the Michigan Department of Civil Rights in order to catalog effective programs and measurement practices. The pledge concludes that these three goals are not the complete answer but are concrete steps toward more equitable workplaces and communities, that working together toward equity can cultivate racially conscious change that anticipates unintended outcomes and does not rely on good intentions but on awareness that all have work to do to dismantle systems of advantage embedded in cultural mindsets and practices that sustain racial inequity, and affirms the value of human diversity and inclusion in all its forms, recognizing that communities have been impacted by racialized messages that contribute to the formation of unconscious biases, and stating opposition to discrimination. Roll call vote: Schmidt yes, Wilson yes, Anne yes, Gottlieb yes, Hammond yes, Hauff yes, Philippart yes. Yes: 7. No: 0.

RESOLUTION 20-065, NAMING OF THE ITT BUILDING. Moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Mrs. Anne. The resolution recites that the Troy School District's mission is to ensure learning for all members of the school community; that the Niles Center housing the Community Education, Adult Education, and Alternative Education programs has come to the end of its useful life; that in September 2019 the Board of Education passed a resolution to purchase and renovate a parcel of property commonly known as 1522 E. Big Beaver Road, Troy, Michigan, Sidwell No. 20-26-200-055, the ITT Building; that renovations have been ongoing since February 2020 and the building is scheduled to open in August 2020; and that Board Policy 6000.08 states the selection of future school names will be left to the discretion of the Board. It resolves that the Troy School District Board of Education names the new building the Troy School District Learning Center, commonly referred to as the Troy Learning Center or TLC. Roll call vote: Philippart yes, Schmidt yes, Wilson yes, Anne yes, Gottlieb yes, Hammond yes, Hauff yes. Yes: 7. No: 0.

SUPERINTENDENT UPDATE. Dr. Machesky provided a brief update on what the Return to School might look like and talked about the Michigan Return to School Roadmap developed by the Governor's office. He shared that TSD Task Force teams have been working on protocols and procedures and learning options and are preparing recommendations that will be brought to the Board for review and discussion the week of August 3rd.

ANNOUNCEMENTS AND ADJOURNMENT. Mr. Schmidt announced that a Special Meeting would be held on Wednesday, August 5th at 4:30 p.m. via Zoom Videoconferencing to discuss options for returning to school in the fall, and that the next regular Board Meeting would be held on August 18th at 7:00 p.m., also via Zoom. The meeting was adjourned at 8:40 p.m. Respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, with the notation GH/jh.
